concepts.label: Ephemeral bucket
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - this page states the single sharpest operational asymmetry between the two types found in this batch: changing an ephemeral bucket's ejection policy needs no restart at all, while changing a Couchbase bucket's does by default

concepts.label: Magma
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - full ejection is the recommended pairing when migrating to this engine

concepts.label: Bucket storage-backend migration
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the multi-step process (change storageBackend, then force a vBucket rewrite via swap rebalance or graceful-failover-plus-recovery) documented in full on the sibling page migrate-bucket.md; introduced here because this page's own noRestart/change-during-migration mechanics only make sense in that context

relations.subject: bucket:couchbase-bucket
relations.evidence: **Value-only**: Couchbase Server removes a document's data, but keeps its keys and metadata in memory.

relations.subject: bucket:couchbase-bucket
relations.evidence: **Full**: Couchbase Server removes the entire document from memory.

relations.subject: bucket:ephemeral-bucket
relations.evidence: **No ejection**: If the bucket reaches its memory quota, the Data Service does not eject data. Instead, it refuses to load any new data until memory becomes available.

relations.subject: bucket:ephemeral-bucket
relations.evidence: **Eject data when RAM is full**: If the bucket approaches its memory quota, the Data Service ejects the least-recently used documents to make space for new data.

relations.subject: bucket:couchbase-bucket
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - changing the ejection policy of a Couchbase bucket via the Web Console triggers a bucket restart by default; the noRestart REST alternative instead requires a swap rebalance or graceful-failover-plus-recovery to complete the change
relations.evidence: When you change the ejection policy of a Couchbase bucket using the Couchbase Server Web Console, Couchbase Server automatically restarts the bucket.

relations.subject: bucket:ephemeral-bucket
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - ephemeral-bucket ejection-policy changes need no restart or follow-on rebalance/failover step at all, unlike Couchbase buckets
relations.evidence: Changing the ejection policy of an ephemeral bucket does not require a bucket restart or other additional steps. The new setting takes effect immediately.

relations.subject: storage-engine:magma
relations.evidence: you should consider changing the bucket's ejection policy to Full Ejection. This policy works well for Magma buckets that have a low memory to storage ratio.

relations.subject: bucket:storage-backend-migration
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - inverted framing: an ejection-policy change made DURING a migration does not take effect until the migration completes
relations.evidence: After you change the ejection policy while migrating the storage backend, the policy does not take effect until you complete the migration.

relations.subject: server/8.0/manage/manage-buckets/change-ejection-policy
relations.evidence: See [Migrate a Bucket's Storage Backend](migrate-bucket.md) for information about migrating a bucket's storage backend and complete steps to change the ejection policy while performing a migration.

notable_absence.finding: The REST section states 'The noRestart parameter has no effect when changing the ejection policy of an ephemeral bucket' - a THIRD independent confirmation in this batch (after create-bucket.md's durability-level list and general-settings.md's auto-reprovisioning settings) that ephemeral buckets follow simpler, disk-persistence-free operational rules than Couchbase buckets. The page never states WHY noRestart is a no-op for ephemeral buckets, but the reason is inferable from bucket:ephemeral-bucket's own promoted description (no disk persistence): a Couchbase-bucket restart exists to let a persisted, disk-backed ejection setting take effect safely, and an ephemeral bucket has nothing on disk to make safe.

cross_component_finding: This page and migrate-bucket.md describe the SAME noRestart REST parameter and the SAME two remediation procedures (swap rebalance; graceful failover + recovery + rebalance) for two conceptually different operations (an ejection-policy change vs. a storage-backend migration) that can nonetheless be triggered TOGETHER in one REST call. This is a genuine mechanism-sharing finding: 'You can change both the storage backend and the ejection policy at the same time' (migrate-bucket.md, cross-referenced from this page's own introduction) - the two settings are independently documented on separate pages but share one underlying apply-and-rewrite mechanism.
